items.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025
items.q: especially because of the Keith Jarrett recordings, which I produced by the way.

ctx.x: Well from Herb Alpert to — Yeah, all these people. It’s amazing. One last thing and I don’t know if I can formulate this question so that you could try to answer it. Does jazz have a role in society now? I feel like it used to and I’m wondering if it still does in your opinion? © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-

I was going to ask you what you think, but I think that as long as people love that music they’re going to want to play it. It’s not about the bread or any of that. I mean there’s plenty of opportunities in commercial music to play good music. But to play jazz, especially the stuff that I like which is straight ahead jazz, you know bebop essentially, but you know I don’t just play bop but we played good bebop with Phil and that was fantastic for me. I knew all the repertoire, and then we got to record and tour…

I’ll close with sort of what you’re talking about. A quote from Phil Woods. He says, “Some couple comes up and says, ‘We were married to ‘Round Trip’ or your music means so much,’ those kinds of comments. Believe me, I’m honored to get prizes and all that, but to have the music mean something to people on that level you can’t buy that man, it ain’t for sale.”
